principles: Reuse the existing DONE post-merge effect and its material-change gate; do not add a parallel bump mechanism
Keep version logic in a pure, testable module (core/version-bump.ts); keep done-effects orchestration thin
Update all 3 version sync points atomically or fail loud — never leave versions drifted
Patch-only, deterministic, idempotent (exactly one increment per qualifying merge)
drivers: rollout-check enforces 3-point version consistency, so all three must update atomically
Must run under the DONE merge-lock and BEFORE the dist rebuild so the rebuilt dist reports the new version
Must not break the DONE merge or leave main dirty / version files corrupted on failure

options.name: bump-in-done-effects-pure-module
pros: Reuses the exact material-change gate (shouldBuildDoneMainPackageForChangedPaths) and the DONE merge-lock
Separate chore:bump commit matches the existing 0.3.x history
Existing post-merge rebuild makes dist report the new version with zero extra build
cons: Adds one commit per qualifying DONE merge
Touches the critical DONE merge code path

options.name: git-post-merge-hook
cons: Git hooks are not committed/shared reliably (project has no husky)
Fires on ALL merges, not just DONE; cannot reuse the material-change gate or merge-lock

options.name: separate-manual-bump-command
cons: Not automatic — defeats the operator intent of a turnkey bump-on-merge

rationale: It reuses the exact gate (material-change) and lock (DONE merge-lock) the operator intent maps to, keeps version logic pure/testable, lands a clean chore:bump commit matching history, and the existing post-merge rebuild makes dist report the new version with zero extra build. Hook/manual options over-fire, cannot be shared, or are not turnkey.

preMortem.scenario: Version files drift out of sync after a partial bump
preMortem.trigger: applyPatchBump writes root package.json then crashes before writing lattice-brand.ts
preMortem.consequence: rollout-check fails on every subsequent run; CLI reports a version mismatch
preMortem.mitigation: applyPatchBump reads all 3 sync points, asserts identical BEFORE writing, computes one nextPatch, writes all 3, re-reads to verify identical; any mismatch throws a clear 3-point-sync recovery message and the DONE merge surfaces it as a loud failure like the build effect

preMortem.trigger: bump fires on a metadata-only DONE merge, or fires twice for one merge
preMortem.consequence: version increments with no code change, or jumps by 2, diluting meaning
preMortem.mitigation: gate strictly on shouldBuildDoneMainPackageForChangedPaths(changedPaths between before/after SHA), identical to the build gate; single call in the single post-merge code path; nextPatch computed from the actual current root version (no accumulation)

preMortem.scenario: The chore:bump commit breaks the DONE merge or leaves main dirty
preMortem.trigger: git add/commit of the version files fails, or the bump writes files but the commit does not run
preMortem.consequence: main worktree left dirty so the next DONE merge clean-tree precheck blocks every story
preMortem.mitigation: bump+commit are a single guarded step in mainMergeRoot under the merge-lock; on commit failure throw a loud error with exact recovery commands (matching runDoneMainPackageBuildAfterMerge failure style); never leave the write uncommitted silently

preMortem.trigger: version-bump.ts imports done-effects.ts for the gate while done-effects imports version-bump
preMortem.mitigation: version-bump.ts exposes pure functions with NO done-effects import; done-effects computes shouldBuild and passes the boolean in; the smoke imports the gate function from done-effects directly since it is not part of the cycle
